Tuning: batching, KV cache, quantization profiles

transcript:
[00:00] Olivia Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do 45 minutes, quick agenda...
[00:12] Maya Patel: sounds good, we have Ethan and Lina from infra today, gonna focus on the numbers
[00:20] Jordan Reyes: awesome, I'll share my screen with the key graphs, note that some labels in the csv got munged so forgive typos
[00:30] Jordan Reyes: alright first slide p50/p95 p99 across the 1k token medium seq test, baseline provider p95 is at ~420ms, our Redwood hosted run with KV cache off is around 380, with KV cache on down to 260ms
[01:05] Ethan Ross: wait 260ms p95? that's with what batch size and hardware?
[01:12] Jordan Reyes: so that was a 8-token steady state batch, model is open-llm-16q quantized profile running on T4-equivalent in the test harness, we also ran a dedicated pool on A100 where p95 dropped to ~190ms
[01:40] Lina Gomez: is the dedicated run identical network path? we saw spikes once traffic crosses our V P C peering
[01:48] Jordan Reyes: good call, dedicated was run in the same region but we used routed peering and a private subnet; we did see an extra ~20ms egress in one test when a cross-region fallback happened
[02:05] Maya Patel: how reproducible are these numbers, like across multiple runs? we need consistent SLOs for production
[02:12] Jordan Reyes: we ran 10 iterations, the variance tightened after warmup--the steady-state 5 runs are in the CSV I'll share. For cold-start the baseline had a big hit on p99 due to model cold load, Redwood's warm pool reduced that by ~30%
[02:40] Olivia Chen: quick context: our focus is to show we can match baseline throughput while lowering p95 and reducing cold-start tail. Jordan, next slide on throughput please
[02:52] Jordan Reyes: throughput graph — tokens/sec under increasing concurrent requests. Baseline provider saturated around 420 tps on these instances, Redwood hosted 480 tps with batching and 560 tps on our dedicated setup with optimized kernels
[03:20] Ethan Ross: curious about cost per token for the dedicated runs versus baseline; those throughput gains may not be worth it if price jumps significantly
[03:30] Olivia Chen: absolutely — we'll include cost-normalized curves in the csv, Jordan will send. Early numbers show dedicated reduces per-token cost by ~12% at scale because of better kernel utilization and batching savings, but committed pricing and capacity matters
[03:52] Lina Gomez: what's included in "committed"? like reserved gpus or reserved throughput?
[03:55] Olivia Chen: typically reserved GPU pool and a committed throughput tier; you get a lower unit cost and SLA on latency/availability
[04:05] Maya Patel: on security — we need SOC2 reports and details on KMS integration and audit logs retention for a private deployment
[04:12] Olivia Chen: we can share SOC2 Type II and our KMS integration patterns — we support customer-managed keys via K M S and H S M integrations. Audit logs are exported to customer S3 or your SIEM, retention is configurable
[04:28] Ethan Ross: do you support SAML SSO and RBAC scoped keys?
[04:32] Jordan Reyes: yes S S O via SAML and fine-grained RBAC; for dedicated and private deployments we can enforce V P C egress only and mutual TLS
[04:40] Maya Patel: good. can you also describe fallback behavior when the dedicated pool hits capacity? we need deterministic behavior for our client-facing endpoints
[04:48] Jordan Reyes: we support smart routing — you can set priority: dedicated -> hosted fallback. If dedicated saturated, requests can be routed to hosted compatible variants with enforced model pinning and a strict latency cap
[05:05] Ethan Ross: what about consistency of model outputs across those variants? we can't have users seeing differing completions between dedicated and hosted variants
[05:12] Olivia Chen: we recommend pinning model versions and using quantization profiles that minimize divergence; Jordan's team runs output-delta evals in the eval harness to ensure regression is within agreed threshold
[05:30] Jordan Reyes: back to tuning — the biggest knobs we used: batching window (ms), max batch size, KV/prefix cache, and quantization profile. For the medium seq test, enabling prefix caching gave the largest p95 improvement
[05:50] Maya Patel: can you explain the prefix cache behavior? we worry about cache invalidation with user-specific contexts
[05:58] Jordan Reyes: prefix/K V cache stores key-values for repeated prompts across sessions; it works best for repeated system prompts or shared instructions. For per-user contexts we either use sharded caches or disable cache to avoid leakage; we've added strict namespace isolation in the private offering
[06:18] Lina Gomez: any risk of PII being stored in the cache? we have to avoid that by design
[06:22] Jordan Reyes: we treat caches as ephemeral and encrypted at rest; customers can configure purging and TTLs, and for regulated PII flows we recommend disabling caching or using dedicated private deploy with customer-managed keying
[06:38] Ethan Ross: the CSV you mentioned — will it include raw latency buckets and request metadata? we need to correlate spikes with network metrics
[06:45] Jordan Reyes: yes full bucketed histograms, request traces with sample ids and a mapping to the infra logs; we'll include a README for columns
[07:00] Maya Patel: ok good. on the bench methodology — was the baseline using identical model checkpoint?
[07:05] Jordan Reyes: same family but not identical checkpoint; baseline used a 16-bit FP checkpoint, our quantized path used 16q and 8q comparisons; we also ran unquantized control runs; notes on checkpoint differences are in the csv header
[07:25] Ethan Ross: so differences in outputs could be from checkpoint and quantization changes, we need to ensure fidelity for clinical summaries
[07:32] Olivia Chen: agreed — for clinical workloads we usually start with a fidelity eval, Jordan's team can run diff-based evals on your prompt set to quantify drift
[07:45] Jordan Reyes: quick demo of a p99 tail event — annotated trace shows a spike caused by a background compaction job on the test node, not model inference. We can schedule compactions off-peak in Dedicated
[08:05] Lina Gomez: good to know. network peering again — we saw intermittent extra 15-40ms when network routing crossed a partner region, will that appear in your hosted numbers?
[08:15] Jordan Reyes: yes hosted numbers include real-world egress; dedicated within your V P C avoids public egress but you still need to account for peering hops. We'll provide a network checklist for latency-sensitive apps
[08:30] Maya Patel: any thoughts on quantization safety for our clinical prompts? we cannot lose hallucination safety
[08:36] Jordan Reyes: quantization per se doesn't change model behavior if done with fidelity-preserving methods; we recommend running your evalops suite (which you have) to measure hallucination delta; we'll help tune profile selection
[08:50] Ethan Ross: you mentioned kernel selection improvements — is that automatic or manual tuning?
[08:55] Jordan Reyes: the runtime auto-selects optimized kernels based on sequence length and host hardware; we also have a compile step for dedicated pools that caches optimized execution paths
[09:08] Olivia Chen: quick q from me — Maya, what are your internal success criteria for this POC?
[09:15] Maya Patel: p95 under 300ms for medium sequences, throughput at least equal to baseline at our 1k qps tests, and end-to-end output fidelity within our accepted regression threshold on the clinical prompt set
[09:30] Olivia Chen: perfect, we'll target that. Jordan, any slides on regression thresholds?
[09:35] Jordan Reyes: yes we'll include delta-eval graphs. For today, higher level notes: Redwood met p95 target on A100 dedicated and got close on hosted with caching; throughput is better on dedicated.
[09:50] Ethan Ross: about the canary/rollout — if we go to production, do you support canary percent rollouts per route?
[09:56] Jordan Reyes: yes route-level rollouts and automatic fallback on errors or latency breaches; we can do canary traffic splits and metric gating
[10:08] Lina Gomez: SLOs/backoff behavior — if Redis or KV cache backend trips, how does runtime degrade?
[10:15] Jordan Reyes: degradation path is to bypass cache and fall back to lower-efficiency execution, which raises latency but maintains correctness; we expose metrics and alerts for cache misses and backend health
[10:32] Maya Patel: let's talk timeline — we want pilot in prod by end of quarter if numbers hold. What's realistic?
[10:39] Olivia Chen: for a dedicated pilot, typical onboarding is 4-6 weeks once we have signed pilot contract and capacity reserved. Hosted pilot could be faster, 1-2 weeks for initial ramp
[10:52] Ethan Ross: network approvals usually take 2-3 weeks from our side, so match that with your steps
[10:58] Olivia Chen: makes sense, we'll align. Jordan, anything else on tunings?
[11:03] Jordan Reyes: one more: batching window had to be tuned down to 12ms to hit p95 targets while preserving throughput. Larger windows boosted throughput but increased tail latency. We documented configs per test in the csv
[11:20] Maya Patel: can you include the exact config snippets we can drop into our infra-as-code?
[11:24] Jordan Reyes: yes, I'll include the YAML snippets for batching, cache TTL, and quantization profile in the runbook
[11:32] Olivia Chen: quick note — we'll redact noisy sample ids in the CSV but keep trace ids for correlation
[11:38] Ethan Ross: good. I have a question about long form tokens — for 4k+ sequences how did Redwood behave?
[11:45] Jordan Reyes: for long sequences our p95 rose predictably; the kernel selection helps but memory management is the limiter; dedicated A100 with larger memory comfortably handled 4k with p95 ~650ms in our test, baseline was around 720ms
[12:05] Maya Patel: ok. let's move to open questions from Astra
[12:10] Lina Gomez: how do you handle data residency in private on-prem installs?
[12:15] Olivia Chen: private on-prem keeps all data in-customer network and supports air-gapped installs; we ship a hardened bundle and we integrate with your K M S. Audit logs stay local unless you opt to export
[12:32] Ethan Ross: what level of support during pilot? we need SRE pairing on first week of rollout
[12:36] Olivia Chen: enterprise pilot includes a solutions engineer and a CSM; Jordan's team offers SRE pairing for the first 2 weeks as part of the pilot scope
[12:48] Maya Patel: ok that covers my main concerns. any blockers from Redwood side?
[12:52] Jordan Reyes: none aside from getting the test creds and network peering details to reproduce the dedicated runs
[13:00] Olivia Chen: recap and next steps — Jordan share full benchmark CSV + YAML runbook by 2026-02-12; Ethan stand up dedicated test creds by 2026-02-17; Olivia to share pricing and SOC2 link by 2026-02-13; Lina to send SRE runbook requirements by 2026-02-16
[13:28] Maya Patel: thanks, we'll review and aim to confirm pilot contract next week
[13:35] Olivia Chen: great, we'll follow up immediately after the CSV is uploaded. thanks everyone
[13:40] Meeting ended
